notes.1a: Most candidates identified the tripod, which was often described as a stand or a Bunsen burner. The condenser caused few problems, although some candidates labelled it as a fractionating column.
notes.1c: The majority of candidates correctly identified the separation method as chromatography.
notes.2a: The table of results was completed correctly by the majority of candidates using the measuring cylinder diagrams. Common errors were with the 20 second and 40 second diagrams.
notes.2b: Most candidates plotted the points on the grid correctly but many candidates did not make their points clear, especially at the origin. Some candidates incorrectly drew a curve through the anomalous point. The first point was often missed and the last point sometimes plotted incorrectly.
notes.2ci: The anomalous point was usually identified correctly. Some candidates thought that the point at 180 s was anomalous because it was the same as the previous volume at 160 s.
notes.2cii: Good responses referred to the misreading of the measuring cylinder or taking the reading too early. References to the point not being on the curve did not answer the question. Many candidates suggested that some gas had escaped without realising that this would have also affected all subsequent results as well. Vague references to human error or recording errors were ignored.
notes.2ciii: This was generally well answered. Some candidates did not clearly show on the grid how the answer was worked out.
notes.2d: Many candidates stated that the reaction had finished but many gave the incorrect reason that all the magnesium had reacted. This showed a lack of understanding as the hydrochloric acid was the limiting reagent.
notes.2ei: A significant number of candidates added the two volumes to get 101 cm instead of subtracting to get 13 cm .
notes.2eii: Many candidates divided by 30 s instead of 20 s, which showed a lack of understanding. Some candidates did not give a unit. Many gave the correct unit of cm / s.
notes.2f: This question was well answered. Most candidates sketched either a steeper curve from the origin or a curve levelling out at the same volume. Better performing candidates did both.
notes.2g: The idea of the reading being caused by air being displaced by the addition of 30 cm of hydrochloric acid was only recognised by the better performing candidates. Many responses referred to the trapping of the air in the measuring cylinder before the acid was added, not appreciating that the diagram at the start of the question showed that the cylinder was full of water. A large number of responses referred to the rapidity of the reaction causing the 30 cm reading, which was incorrect.
notes.2h: Most correct responses referred to accuracy as the problem when using a measuring cylinder and suggested replacing it with a gas syringe, burette or pipette. References to repeating the experiment and taking the average of the results were also seen. Some candidates did not following the instruction to explain their suggested improvement. References to speeding up the reaction by using powdered magnesium or raising the temperature were common incorrect answers.
notes.3b: Many candidates identified solution T as iron( III ) nitrate. Some mistakenly thought that the ammonia formed in the third test indicated the presence of ammonium ions. Incorrect responses such as transition element, calcium or zinc ions, and iodide or chloride ions were prevalent.
